import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1043

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1043](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1043)
- [EHP58] Erdős, P. and Herzog, F. and Piranian, G., Metric properties of polynomials. J.
  Analyse Math. (1958), 125-148.
- [Po59] Pommerenke, Ch., On some problems by Erdős, Herzog and Piranian. Michigan Math. J.
  (1959), 221-225.
- [Po61] Pommerenke, Ch., On metric properties of complex polynomials. Michigan Math. J. (1961),
  97-115.
-/

namespace Erdos1043

open MeasureTheory Polynomial

attribute [local instance] Measure.Subtype.measureSpace

/-- The set $\{ z \in \mathbb{C} : \lvert f(z)\rvert\leq 1\}$ -/
def levelSet (f : Polynomial ℂ) : Set ℂ :=
  {z : ℂ | ‖f.eval z‖ ≤ 1}

/--
**Erdős Problem 1043**:
Let $f\in \mathbb{C}[x]$ be a monic polynomial.
Must there exist a straight line $\ell$ such that the projection of
$$\{ z: \lvert f(z)\rvert\leq 1\}$$
onto $\ell$ has measure at most $2$?

Pommerenke [Po61] proved that the answer is no.

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev using Aristotle.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 28 30,
formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.24.0/ErdosProblems/Erdos1043.lean",
formal_proof using formal_conjectures at "https://github.com/XC0R/formal-conjectures/blob/7db17471701f15b125d1c36bc1fa5bb9b702d6be/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/1043.lean#L214"]
theorem erdos_1043 :
    answer(False) ↔ ∀ (f : ℂ[X]), f.Monic → f.degree ≥ 1 →
      ∃ (u : ℂ), ‖u‖ = 1 ∧
      volume ((ℝ ∙ u).orthogonalProjectionOnto '' levelSet f) ≤ 2 := by
  sorry

/--
On the other hand, Pommerenke also proved there always exists a line such that the projection has
measure at most 3.3.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 28 30]
theorem erdos_1043.variants.weak :
    ∀ (f : ℂ[X]), f.Monic → f.degree ≥ 1 →
      ∃ (u : ℂ), ‖u‖ = 1 ∧
      volume ((ℝ ∙ u).orthogonalProjectionOnto '' levelSet f) ≤ 3.3 := by
  sorry

end Erdos1043

findings.description: The local `Measure.Subtype.measureSpace` instance at line 35 makes the `volume` in line 58 the restriction of ambient two-dimensional Lebesgue measure on ℂ to the line subtype, not length along that line. Its definition is `Measure.comap Subtype.val volume`. Every real span of one complex vector has zero ambient volume, so every projected set in this statement has measure zero. Taking `u = 1` therefore proves the entire right-hand side for every polynomial, making `answer(False) ↔ ...` false. An independent Lean proof of the negation of this statement is in `/workspace/review/scratch.lean`, with no `sorryAx` dependency.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/1043 asks whether every monic non-constant complex polynomial has a straight-line projection of its closed unit sublevel set with measure at most 2. Pommerenke, [Po61], §3, pp. 102–103, explicitly calls this 'linear measure' and constructs a lemniscate domain whose minimum projection measure exceeds 2.386.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove `attribute [local instance] Measure.Subtype.measureSpace`. Mathlib then selects `measureSpaceOfInnerProductSpace` on `(ℝ ∙ u)`, giving intrinsic one-dimensional Lebesgue measure. Keep the negative answer. Alternatively, measure the real-coordinate image `{Re(z * conj u) | z ∈ levelSet f}` using Lebesgue measure on ℝ.

findings.description: The `volume` in line 69 uses the same ambient-restriction subtype instance rather than intrinsic length. Consequently the measured projection is always zero, and the conclusion holds for every set in ℂ, without either polynomial hypothesis and even with upper bound 0. This trivial zero-area statement does not express Pommerenke's projection-length bound. The scratch file proves this trivialization; it also verifies that, with the corrected intrinsic measure, the projection for the admissible polynomial `X` has measure 2 rather than 0.
findings.source_evidence: The concluding remark at https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/1043 says that there always exists a line whose projection has measure at most 3.3. Pommerenke [Po61], Theorem 7, pp. 103–104, proves that a closed bounded set of capacity 1 has a projection of linear measure less than 3.30; p. 97 explains the capacity-one normalization for monic polynomial lemniscates.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the local subtype-measure instance at line 35, letting the line carry its canonical intrinsic Lebesgue measure. The existing quantifiers, positive-degree restriction, and bound `3.3` can remain unchanged.

findings.description: The main docstring says only 'a monic polynomial', omitting the non-constant restriction explicitly present in the source and encoded by `f.degree ≥ 1`. Taken literally, the docstring admits `f = 1`, whose level set is all of ℂ and whose projections have infinite length, making the negative answer trivial.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/1043 begins: 'Let f ∈ ℂ[x] be a monic non-constant polynomial.' The Lean theorem includes `f.degree ≥ 1`.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the main docstring to say 'a monic non-constant polynomial'.

reformulations.difference: The line parameterization itself is harmless: Lean searches over real spans of unit complex vectors, hence lines through the origin, whereas the source allows arbitrary affine straight lines. This is separate from the measure defect above.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: With intrinsic length, projection onto an affine line a + L is π_L(z) + (a − π_L(a)). Its image is therefore a translate of the projection onto L and has exactly the same length. Every real one-dimensional direction L has a unit generator u, obtained by normalizing any nonzero vector in L. Thus the two searches are equivalent once the measure is corrected.

reformulations.difference: The weak variant likewise uses unit-vector linear spans instead of arbitrary affine lines; this parameterization does not require changing.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Affine translation of the target line only translates the projected set, preserving intrinsic one-dimensional Lebesgue measure. Normalizing a nonzero direction vector does not change its span. Hence existence of a projection with intrinsic length at most 3.3 is equivalent for these two line parameterizations, independently of the separate measure-instance error.

The required compile command succeeds with only the expected sorry warnings; fresh-source checks confirm the corrected measure instances and projection length 2 for the polynomial X.
